get.summary: Lists your API keys, or every key for an admin. Keys themselves are never shown again.

post.summary: Creates an API key acting as you. The key is only in this response.

get.summary: Lists every delete, unmonitor and mark played, newest first.

post.summary: Signs this browser in: sets an HttpOnly session cookie for a personal device, from an API key or a paired device token.

delete.summary: Signs this browser out: revokes its device and clears the cookie.

get.summary: Retrieves the newest build of an app (android, linux or what the server configures) the server holds, without asking its source. 404 when there is none.

post.summary: Asks the app's update source for a newer build and downloads it, then retrieves the newest build. 503 when the source fails.

get.summary: Sends the file of the newest build of an app, with range requests to resume.

head.summary: Sends the file of the newest build of an app, with range requests to resume.

get.summary: Lists your devices, or every device for an admin.

delete.summary: Revokes a device and every token it holds.

post.summary: Returns a url for any item's artwork without a credential in it, for clients that store artwork urls in their own library. It only opens artwork and stops working when the device is revoked.

get.summary: Lists the events after a sequence, for a client that was offline.
get.description:
Event types, with the schema of their payload:
library.item.added, library.item.updated, library.item.removed (LibraryItemPayload),
library.file.replaced (FileReplacedPayload), watchstate.changed (WatchStatePayload, only to that user),
trackpreference.changed (TrackPreferencePayload, only to that user), scan.progress (ScanProgressPayload),
action.completed (ActionCompletedPayload), subtitle.request.updated (SubtitleRequestModel, only to that user),
playback.started, playback.stopped (PlaybackPayload, only to that user).
playback.progress (PlaybackPayload, only to that user) is not in this list: the WebSocket alone sends it, with
sequence 0, while a session plays, at most every 5 seconds per session.
Page with since set to the sequence of the last item while hasMore is true, then continue from latest.
When resync is true the events are gone: reload what is shown and continue from latest.

get.summary: Opens a WebSocket that replays the events after since, sends stream.ready, then every event as it happens.
get.description:
Messages have the shape of EventMessage. stream.ready carries the sequence the client is now at.
stream.resync means the missed events are gone or too many: reload what is shown, the sequence is where to continue.
Neither is stored. The server closes with 1001 when the client fell too far behind and with 1008 when its
credential was revoked or expired; on 1001 or a dropped connection, reconnect with since set to the last sequence.
With remote=true the device can be controlled from the caller's other devices (/remote): it then also gets
remote.command messages (RemoteCommandPayload), sequence 0 and never stored, which it carries out. Every socket of a
user gets playback.progress (PlaybackPayload), sequence 0 and never stored, at most every 5 seconds per playing session.

get.summary: Retrieves a version of an item with its tracks and chapters.
Streams a version over HTTP, with range requests for seeking.

head.summary: Streams a version over HTTP, with range requests for seeking.

get.summary: Sends a version as a file to save, under its name on disk, with range requests to resume. Starts no playback.

head.summary: Sends a version as a file to save, under its name on disk, with range requests to resume. Starts no playback.

get.summary: Serves an external subtitle file of a version.
Retrieves the seek thumbnails of a version: their layout and the urls of the sheets. 404 until they are made.
Retrieves the seek thumbnails as a WebVTT track, each interval pointing at its tile with #xywh.
Retrieves one sheet of seek thumbnails.
Serves a text subtitle of a version, embedded or external, converted to WebVTT for browsers.
Retrieves the server version and database status.

post.summary: Deletes the files of a movie, episode, season or series in the named instances, and unmonitors it unless told not to.
post.description:
scope must be the item's own type, deleteFiles and unmonitor are both required, and instances names every
instance that acts. search, with deleteFiles true and unmonitor false, fetches a new copy. dryRun answers what
would happen without doing it. Answers 502 with the outcome when every instance failed. Admins only, unless
usersMayRemove is on.

post.summary: Unmonitors a movie, episode, season or series in the named instances and keeps its files.
Marks an item played or unplayed for you, with every episode below a season or series.

get.summary: Lists movies and series, or all items of one type.
Lists the first letters of the titles, A to Z, with where each starts in the A to Z list, for jumping to one.
Retrieves a movie, series, season or episode.
Lists the seasons of a series or the episodes of a season.
Retrieves an image of an item, through Radarr or Sonarr.
get.description:
size medium or small asks for the smaller copy Radarr, Sonarr or TMDB keep (a poster 500 or 250 pixels high, a backdrop 360
or 180), and gives the original where there is none. Leave it out for the original. The answer carries an ETag, and a
request with it in If-None-Match gets a 304 while the picture is the same.

get.summary: Lists what you started and did not finish, most recent first.
Lists the next episode of every series you are watching.

post.summary: Starts a full sync with Radarr and Sonarr, to look for new movies and series now.
post.description: Answers at once. The sync runs in the background and ends with a scan.progress event of kind sync, after the library events of what it changed. Asking while a sync is already waiting to start queues nothing more.

get.summary: Lists the switched on bridges: the apps that connect through one, how they connect and the address to give them.

post.summary: Makes a link for you and one bridge, such as an add-on url. The token is in this response only, revoke it under devices.

get.summary: Lists the urls that get events, with how their deliveries go.

post.summary: Adds a url that gets every event from now on, or the types named. The signing secret is only in this response.
post.description:
Each delivery is a POST of { sequence, type, version, payload, createdAt, userId } with X-Akira-Event, X-Akira-Delivery
(the sequence) and X-Akira-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "t.body" with the secret>. Deliveries
come in sequence order; a failing receiver is retried with a growing delay and later events wait behind it.

patch.summary: Changes the name, url, event types or whether it is on. A failing webhook is tried again right away.

post.summary: Replaces the signing secret. The new one is only in this response.
Sends a webhook.test delivery now and answers what the receiver said.
Starts pairing a new device. Show the code to the user and poll for the token.

get.summary: Lists devices waiting to be approved.

post.summary: Polls a pairing: 202 while it waits, 200 with the device token once approved (only once).
Approves a code as a personal device (yours, or anyone's as admin) or as a shared device (admin).
Denies a waiting code.

get.summary: Lists who can sign in with their PIN. Only on the home network.

post.summary: Signs this device in as a user who gives their PIN, as a personal device. Only on the home network.
post.description:
At home is the local network directly, or through a proxy listed in Proxy:TrustedProxies that names a local client.
Wrong PINs count towards the same lockout as on shared devices. The token answers like a completed pairing.

post.summary: Chooses the version, sources and tracks for this client and opens a playback session.

get.summary: Lists what is playing now, on which device, how it is delivered and how a transcode keeps up.

post.summary: Reports the position, about every 10 seconds and on pause and seek.
Reports that the user changed audio or subtitles, which is remembered for the series or movie.
Ends the session and marks the item played past the threshold.

get.summary: Retrieves the master playlist of a session whose plan offered an hls source.
Retrieves the media playlist: every segment of the version, segment n starting at n times the segment length.
Retrieves a segment, transcoded on demand. A segment far from the last one, a seek, starts the transcode there.
Lists the plugins that loaded, built in or from the plugins folder, with their settings (never the values) and the DLLs that did not load.
Lists the profiles this device can use.

post.summary: Picks a profile on a shared device and returns a session token for it.

get.summary: Lists the caller's other devices that can be controlled now, with what each plays.
get.description: A device can be controlled while it has the event WebSocket open with remote=true, signed in as the caller.

post.summary: Sends a command to one of the caller's devices: play an item, pause, resume, seek or stop.
post.description:
The device gets it at once as a remote.command message on its event WebSocket. It is not stored: a device that is
not connected never gets it, which is a 404. play needs itemId (and fromStart to ignore the resume point), seek
needs positionMs.

get.summary: Retrieves what removing does by default per type, and whether users other than admins may remove.

put.summary: Sets what removing does by default per type, and whether users other than admins may remove.

get.summary: Retrieves your override, what removing does for you, and whether you may remove at all.
get.description:
A client shows the effective behavior in its confirmation and sends the matching action: deleteAndUnmonitor is
delete with deleteFiles and unmonitor true, deleteKeepMonitored is delete with unmonitor false and search true,
unmonitorOnly is unmonitor.

put.summary: Sets your override. A type left empty follows the server default.

get.summary: Tells whether the first admin still has to be created.

post.summary: Creates the first admin with the setup code from the server log, and returns an API key for it.

get.summary: Serves what a signed url from a bridge points at: a file with range requests, a WebVTT subtitle or artwork.

head.summary: Serves what a signed url from a bridge points at: a file with range requests, a WebVTT subtitle or artwork.

get.summary: Lists what can be done for a language: tracks the version has, downloads, and tracks to translate from.
get.description: fileId picks the version, the first one otherwise. Sources that fail are listed in problems, the rest still answers.

post.summary: Asks for a subtitle the file does not have yet. Progress arrives as subtitle.request.updated events.
post.description:
optionId is one from subtitle-options; without it the server picks a track the file has, then a download, then a
translation. sessionId ties the result to a playback, so the finished event carries the track to load into it.
An open request for the same file and language is returned instead of starting a second one.

get.summary: Lists your latest subtitle requests, or everyone's for an admin.
Retrieves a subtitle request with its progress, and the new track once it is done.

post.summary: Stops a queued or running subtitle request.

get.summary: Lists the subtitle sources and translators and whether each is configured.
Retrieves the rules of a movie or episode, or of the whole series for a series or season, and what applies.

put.summary: Sets those rules. A field left out falls back to the series or global rules.

delete.summary: Forgets those rules and the remembered tracks, so the global rules apply again.

get.summary: Retrieves your global rules and every series or item you set or remembered something for.
Tells whether this server has a Trakt app, and whether your account is linked or waiting for its code.

delete.summary: Unlinks your Trakt account. What was imported stays.

post.summary: Starts linking your Trakt account. Enter pending.userCode at pending.verificationUrl, then poll.
Asks Trakt whether you entered the code, every pending.intervalSeconds. Linked imports your watched history.
Marks played what Trakt says you watched. It only adds plays, nothing becomes unplayed.

get.summary: Retrieves the signed in user and the device the request came from.

put.summary: Sets, changes or removes your own PIN. Changing an existing PIN needs the current one.

get.summary: Lists every user.

post.summary: Creates a user.

patch.summary: Renames a user or changes their role.

delete.summary: Deletes a user with their devices, sessions and API keys.

put.summary: Sets or removes a user's PIN.

post.summary: Adds watch state from another server to your own, matched on TMDB, TVDB or IMDb ids, at most 1000 entries a call. It never makes anything unplayed, keeps a position watched here more recently, and changes nothing with dryRun.
Receives a Radarr or Sonarr webhook and refreshes the movie or series it is about.
post.description: Set up as a Webhook connection in Radarr or Sonarr, with the instance's WebhookSecret as the password.

ActionCompletedPayload.description:
Represents the payload of the event sent when a delete or unmonitor finished. Instances are the keys of the
instances that acted.

ActionResult.description: Represents the outcome of a delete or unmonitor, per instance. AuditId is null on a dry run, which is not recorded.

ApiKeySummary.description: Represents an API key without the key itself. Prefix is the start of the key, to tell keys apart.

ApprovePairingRequest.description:
Represents the body of a request to approve a pairing code. UserId is the owner of a personal device, the approver
when null, and stays null for a shared device.

ArtworkLink.description:
Represents a url for any item's artwork. UrlTemplate has {itemId} and {kind} (an image kind) to fill in, and needs
no credential.

AuditEntryModel.description:
Represents one entry of the audit log. Details is the request and the outcome per instance as JSON, and the entry
stays when its user, device or item is deleted.

BridgeSummary.description:
Represents a switched on bridge and how its app connects. Address is the bridge's base url as the caller reached the
server, what an Address bridge's app is given.

BrowserSessionRequest.description:
Represents the body of a request to sign a browser in. Name and Platform describe a browser signing in with an API
key, which becomes a new device. A paired browser keeps its own.

CapabilitiesModel.description:
Represents what a client says it can play. A list left out means the client did not say, so anything goes.
AccessModes names filePath, http or hls.

ChapterSummary.description: Represents a chapter of a file. EndMs is null when the file gives no end.

ClientUpdateModel.description: Represents the newest build of a client app the server holds. An app installs it when Build is higher than its own.

CreateApiKeyRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to create an API key.

CreatedApiKey.description: Represents a new API key. Key is only in this response and never shown again.

CreatedOutgoingWebhook.description: Represents a webhook with its signing secret. The secret is only in this response, and in the one after rotating it.

CreateLinkRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to make a link for one bridge. Name defaults to the bridge's name.

CreateOutgoingWebhookRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to create a webhook. EventTypes empty or left out is every event.

CreateSubtitleRequest.description:
Represents the body of a request for a subtitle a file does not have yet. Without OptionId the server picks one, and
SessionId ties the result to a playback.

CreateUserRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to create a user. Pin is optional, a user can be created without one.

CurrentUser.description:
Represents the signed in user and the device the request came from. Credential is device, profile or apiKey, and
Device is null for an API key.

DeleteActionRequest.description:
Represents the body of a request to delete the files of an item. Scope, DeleteFiles, Unmonitor and Instances are all
required, and Search needs DeleteFiles true and Unmonitor false.

DenyPairingRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to deny a waiting pairing code.

DeviceSummary.description: Represents a personal or shared device, or a link. UserId is null for a shared device, its users pick a profile.

DownloadOption.description: Represents a subtitle a source can download. HashMatch is true when it was made for this exact file.

EffectiveRemoval.description: Represents what removing does for each type of item, with every type filled in.

EffectiveRulesModel.description: Represents the track rules that apply once the item, series, global and server rules are combined.

EventMessage.description:
Represents one event as a client receives it. Sequence is 0 for a message that is never stored, such as a remote
command.

EventPage.description:
Represents one page of the events after a sequence. Latest is where to continue from, and Resync is true when the
events asked for are gone.

ExistingSubtitle.description: Represents a subtitle track in the asked language that the version already has.

ExternalIds.description: Represents the TMDB, TVDB and IMDb ids of an item.

FileDetail.description: Represents a version of an item, the file one instance has, with its tracks and chapters.

FileReplacedPayload.description: Represents the payload of the event sent when a sync found an item's file in an instance replaced by a new one.

HealthResponse.description:
Represents the health of the server. Status follows the database only, since without ffprobe files just stay
unprobed.

InstanceOutcome.description:
Represents what a delete or unmonitor did in one instance. Files and Bytes are what the instance holds for the item,
FilesAlreadyGone the files it no longer had when asked to delete them, and Error says why it failed, or on a dry run
why it would.

ItemDetail.description:
Represents a movie, series, season or episode with its versions, the instances that hold it and
the user's watch state.

ItemImage.description:
Represents an image of an item. BlurHash is what a client draws while the image loads, null until
the server has made it.

ItemInfo.description:
Represents the ratings, genres, certification and trailer of an item. Scores are out of 10, IMDb and
TMDB from Radarr, Rating from Sonarr. An episode or season has its series' genres and certification.

ItemInstance.description: Represents an instance that holds an item, which a delete or unmonitor names. A series has no versions of its own.

ItemLetter.description:
Represents a first letter of the titles. Offset is where its first title is in the A to Z list,
Count how many it has.

ItemLettersResponse.description:
Represents the first letters of the titles, for jumping in the A to Z list. Total is the count of
all titles that match.

ItemSummary.description: Represents a movie, series, season or episode as a list shows it, without its versions.

ItemTrackPreferences.description:
Represents the track rules of a movie, episode or series and what applies. RemembersAudio and
RemembersSubtitle are true when a track the user picked during playback is remembered.

ItemVersion.description: Represents a version of an item, the file one instance holds, with its video, audio and subtitle tracks.

LibraryItemPayload.description:
Represents the payload of the event sent when a library item was added, updated or removed. SeriesId is the series a
series, season or episode belongs to.

LibrarySyncReceipt.description: Represents the answer to a request for a library sync. Queued is false when a sync was already waiting to start.

LinkCreated.description:
Represents a new link for a bridge. Token is shown once. Url is what the app installs, with the token in it, and
AppUrl opens it in the app.

MarkPlayedRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to mark an item played or unplayed. Played is required.

MarkPlayedResult.description:
Represents the outcome of marking an item played or unplayed. Items counts what was marked, the episodes below a
season or series included.

NowPlaying.description:
Represents a playback session that is running now. Delivery is direct (the client opens the file,
by path or over HTTP) or hls (the server segments it).

NowPlayingDevice.description: Represents the device a playback session plays on.

NowPlayingTrack.description: Represents the audio or subtitle track a playback session plays.

NowPlayingUser.description: Represents the user a playback session plays for.

NowPlayingVersion.description:
Represents the version a playback session plays. Instance is the name of the instance that holds it,
and Hdr is hdr10, dolbyvision or hlg, null for SDR or a file not probed yet.

OutgoingWebhookDelivery.description:
Represents the body of every webhook delivery. UserId is set on events that belong to one user, such as playback and
watch state.

OutgoingWebhookSummary.description:
Represents a webhook and how its deliveries go. LastSequence is the last event it handled, and
EventTypes empty is every event.

OutgoingWebhookTestResult.description: Represents what came of a test delivery to a webhook, with the receiver's status code when it answered.

PagedResponseOfAuditEntryModel.description: Represents one page of items. Total is the count of all items that match, not only this page.

PagedResponseOfItemSummary.description: Represents one page of items. Total is the count of all items that match, not only this page.

PairingCompleted.description: Represents a device that finished pairing or signed in with a PIN. Token is its device token, handed out only once.

PairingPending.description: Represents a pairing that still waits to be approved, the answer to a poll until then.

PairingStarted.description:
Represents a pairing that has started. Code is shown to the user, and the device polls with PollSecret every
PollIntervalSeconds until ExpiresAt.

PendingPairing.description: Represents a device waiting to be approved, as an admin sees it in the list.

PinSignInRequest.description:
Represents the body of a request to sign a device in as a user who gives their PIN. The other fields describe the
new personal device.

PinUser.description: Represents a user who can sign in with their PIN.

PlanItem.description: Represents the movie or episode a playback is for, with the series title for an episode.

PlanMarker.description:
Represents a part a player can offer to skip, an intro, credits, a recap or the preview of the next episode.
Source says whether the chapters or an audio fingerprint found it.

PlanSource.description: Represents a way a client can open the version. Mode is filePath with a Path, or http or hls with a Url.

PlanTrack.description: Represents an audio or subtitle track of a version, with what a client finds it by.

PlanTranscode.description:
Represents what the hls source changes, null when the version goes out as it is. Video is copy or
h264, audio copy, aac or ac3. BurnedSubtitleStreamId is the subtitle drawn into the picture, which
the client then does not show itself.

PlanVersion.description:
Represents the version a playback plan chose. Reason is requested, only-version or best-match, and
IsCompatible is false when the client cannot decode its video or show its HDR.

PlaybackPayload.description:
Represents the payload of the event sent when a playback session opened (a plan was made) or ended. Transcoding says
the version goes out as HLS.

PlaybackPlan.description:
Represents the version, sources and tracks a client plays an item with, in the session it opened.
TrickplayUrl is null until the file has trickplay thumbnails.

PlaybackPlanRequest.description: Represents the body of a request for a playback plan. FileId picks the version, the server chooses one otherwise.

PluginOverview.description:
Represents the plugins of the server. Path is the folder plugins are loaded from, and Skipped are
DLLs in it that did not load, with why.

PluginSettingKind.description: Defines the kinds of value a plugin setting holds. User is the name of an Akira user or profile.

PluginSettingModel.description: Represents a setting of a plugin. Values are never returned, only whether one is set.

PluginSummary.description:
Represents a loaded plugin. Source is "built-in" or the DLL's file name, and Provides lists what it
registered, such as subtitleSource.

PollPairingRequest.description: Represents the body of a poll for a pairing's token. PollSecret is the one the pairing started with.

ProfileSession.description: Represents a session for a profile picked on a shared device, with its token.

ProfileSummary.description: Represents a profile a device can use. HasPin says whether picking it needs a PIN.

ProgressRequest.description: Represents the body of a report of the playback position and whether it is paused.

RemoteCommandPayload.description:
Represents the payload of a remote.command message, a command the device carries out. FromDeviceId
is the device that sent it.

RemoteCommandRequest.description:
Represents the body of a request to send a command to a device. Play needs ItemId, FromStart
ignores the resume point, and Seek needs PositionMs.

RemoteDevice.description: Represents one of the caller's devices that can be controlled now, with what it plays.

RemoteNowPlaying.description:
Represents what a device that can be controlled plays. While it plays, PositionMs moves on by the
time since the last report. Markers are the plan's, so a remote shows up next when the player does.

RemovalBehaviors.description: Represents a user's own choice of what removing does per type. A null type follows the server default.

items.description: Represents the outcome of a sync in one instance, with the counts of items it added, updated and unlinked.

ScanProgressPayload.description:
Represents the payload of the event sent after a sync, refresh or probe. Instances and Removed are only filled by a
sync or refresh, Probed, Missing and Failed only by a probe.

ServerRemovalSettings.description: Represents what removing does by default per type, and whether users other than admins may remove.

SetPinRequest.description:
Represents the body of a request to set, change or remove a PIN. A null NewPin removes it, and CurrentPin is needed
to change your own existing PIN.

SetupRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to create the first admin. SetupCode is in the server log, and Pin is optional.

SetupResponse.description: Represents the first admin that setup created and an API key for it.

SetupStatus.description: Represents whether the first admin still has to be created.

SkippedPluginModel.description: Represents a DLL in the plugin folder that did not load, with why.

StartPairingRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to start pairing a new device, which it describes.

StartProfileSessionRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to pick a profile on a shared device. Pin is needed when the profile has one.

StopRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to end a playback session, with the last position.

StreamPayload.description:
Represents the payload of the stream.ready and stream.resync messages of the event socket. Latest is the sequence
the client is now at.

StreamSummary.description:
Represents a video, audio or subtitle track of a file. Id is the stable track id, never the ffprobe index, and
EventCount is the number of lines of a subtitle track.

SubtitleOptionsResponse.description: Represents what can be done for a subtitle language of a version. Problems lists the sources that failed.

SubtitleProviderModel.description: Represents a subtitle source or translator. Kind is source or translator.

SubtitleRequestModel.description:
Represents a request for a subtitle a file does not have yet. Progress runs from 0 to 100, and Track
is the new track once the request is completed.

TrackMatch.description:
Represents what a client finds a track by. Flags holds default, forced, hearingImpaired, commentary or descriptive,
and IndexHint is the ffprobe index, only a hint.

TrackPick.description:
Represents the audio or subtitle track a playback plan picked. StreamId and Match are null when nothing is picked,
the reason says why.

TrackPreferenceOverride.description:
Represents the rules or remembered tracks a user has for one series or item. ItemId and Title are
null when the library does not have it.

TrackPreferenceOverview.description:
Represents a user's track rules. Global is the user's own, ServerDefault the household's from the configuration,
Effective what applies when neither an item nor a series says otherwise.

TrackPreferencePayload.description:
Represents the payload of the event sent when a user's track preferences changed. IdentityKey is the series or item
they belong to, and null for the global ones.

TrackRulesModel.description: Represents a set of track rules. A field left null falls back to the series, global or server rules.

TracksRequest.description:
Represents the body of a report that the user changed audio or subtitles. Send SubtitleStreamId or
SubtitlesOff, not both.

TraktImportResult.description: Represents how many movies and episodes an import from Trakt marked played.

TraktPending.description:
Represents a Trakt link that waits for the user to enter UserCode at VerificationUrl. Poll every
IntervalSeconds until ExpiresAt.

TraktStatus.description:
Represents the Trakt link of a user. Configured says whether this server has a Trakt app at all, and Pending is set
while a link waits for the user on Trakt's site.

TranscoderSample.description: Represents one reading of how fast a transcode runs, its speed against realtime and its frames per second.

TranscoderStats.description:
Represents how a transcode keeps up. Speed is against realtime (1 keeps up), EncodedToMs how far into the file the
transcode got. History is the last few minutes.

TranslationOption.description: Represents a subtitle track a translator can translate from. Reason says why not when Translatable is false.

TrickplayModel.description:
Represents the trickplay thumbnails of a file. There is one thumbnail every IntervalMs, laid out row
by row on sheets of Columns by Rows tiles, Count thumbnails in all.

UnmonitorActionRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to unmonitor an item and keep its files. Scope and Instances are both required.

UpdateOutgoingWebhookRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to change a webhook. A field left out stays as it is.

UpdateUserRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to rename a user or change their role. A null field stays as it is.

UserRemovalSettings.description: Represents a user's removal override, what removing does for them, and whether they may remove at all.

UserState.description: Represents a user's watch state of an item.

UserSummary.description: Represents a user with their role and whether they have a PIN.

VersionTrack.description: Represents an audio or subtitle track of a version. IsExternal is true for a file next to the video.

VersionVideo.description: Represents the video track of a version.

WatchStateImportEntry.description:
Represents the watch state of one movie or episode to import. For an episode the ids are its series' ids, with the
season and episode number.

WatchStateImportRequest.description: Represents the body of a request to import watch state. With DryRun nothing is changed.

WatchStateImportResult.description:
Represents the result of a watch state import. Unmatched holds the places in the request of the
entries Akira could not key on.

WatchStatePayload.description:
Represents the payload of the event sent when a user's watch state of an item changed. Reason is progress (a pause
or resume), stop (the end of a playback), marked (played or unplayed by hand) or imported (from another server).

WebhookReceipt.description:
Represents the answer to a received Radarr or Sonarr webhook. Queued is false when it needed no refresh or the queue
